title: The Hostel Kitchen
story: Imani arrived at the hostel in the evening and received a key from the front desk. Her room had a bunk and a small lamp, but no place to cook. A sign in the hall said guests could use the shared kitchen until ten. Imani was hungry after the long bus ride, so she carried her food box downstairs. The kitchen had two cookers, a sink, and a long table. A guest called Rafi was boiling pasta and singing quietly. She washed a pan and set it on the free cooker. She had rice, eggs, and a few vegetables from the market. While the rice cooked, she cut the vegetables on a board and kept the knife away from the edge. Rafi offered her a little salt and asked where she was from. At nine Imani realised she had used Rafi's wooden spoon and had not asked. She washed it at once and said sorry. Rafi smiled and said sharing was normal in a hostel kitchen if you cleaned up. Imani put her leftovers in a box with her name on the lid. She wiped the table, washed the pan, and hung the cloth on a hook. Before she left, she checked that the cooker was off. Upstairs, the room felt more welcoming because dinner was done and the kitchen was ready for the next person. Imani wrote a short note to herself: clean, label, and switch off.
